newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Revival of murder case shakes up Dominican army.
newsitem.headline: Revival of murder case shakes up Dominican army.

text.p: Renewed interest in the case of a politically active professor who disappeared two years ago is causing a stir in the upper ranks of the Dominican military.

Authorities on Thursday night banned Major General Constantino Matos Villanueva, a former armed forces secretary, from leaving the country pending a probe into the 1994 disappearance of Narcisco Gonzalez, a journalist and leftist activist and law professor at the University of Santo Domingo.
Attorney-General Abel Rodriguez del Orbe imposed the order on Matos Villanueva after learning he wanted to travel to a South American country.
Matos Villanueva protested his innocence on Friday.
He said he had investigated Gonzalez' disappearance at the time but could find no one to hold responsible.
"At the time the country was in much confusion," he told reporters."I have nothing to do with the Gonzalez case and I only hope that I can say that in court."
Rodriguez del Orbe also banned others possibly involved in the case from leaving, including more ex-military officers.
Gonzalez disappeared in May 1994. His family maintains he was kidnapped by the military and killed.

The incident followed publication of an article in a magazine seen as insulting to then President Joaquin Balaguer. One day earlier Gonzalez had made a speech at the university accusing army generals of corruption.
The case resurfaced this week after President Leonel Fernandez on Monday retired 24 generals, including Matos Villanueva, who was armed forces secretary when Gonzalez disappeared.
The government said the generals, most of whom were close to Balaguer, were retired to trim the top-heavy military and cut state expenses.
On Thursday, the current armed forces secretary, Lieutenant General Juan Bautista Rojas Tabar, urged Fernandez to act against other generals who he said were responsible for the disappearance.
